tip: gav honom = gave him. The person receiving comes right after the verb, with no 'to' needed.
Yes/no questions put the verb first: Borde vi inte vänta? = Shouldn't we wait?
When 'what' is the subject of an indirect clause, add som: vad som hände = what happened.
Unlike English 'that,' att is normally kept in reported speech: viskade att han hade en hemlighet.
Så fort means 'as soon as.' The following main clause inverts: Så fort jag kom hem somnade jag.
borde (should) is a modal, so the next verb is a plain infinitive with no att: borde gå bra.
After börja, att before the next verb is optional: började jobba = started working.
fick, the past of få, often means 'had to': vi fick beställa pizza = we had to order pizza.
bli means 'become,' used for future states: det ska bli spännande = it will be exciting.
vore is the 'would be' form of vara, for hypotheticals: det vore trevligt = it would be nice.
After föreslog att (suggested that), Swedish uses skulle: föreslog att vi skulle vänta.
skynda sig means to hurry; it needs the reflexive pronoun: vi måste skynda oss.
ta sig tid = make time; the reflexive dig is required: du tog dig tid.
vänta sig means to expect, not just wait: hade inte väntat mig det = hadn't expected it.
bestämma sig = make up your mind; use the reflexive: vi måste bestämma oss.
passa sig means watch out, and it is reflexive: Passa dig.
sin means 'his/her own,' pointing back to the subject: skriver brev till sin familj.
sin/sitt/sina all mean 'one's own'; sitt is the ett-word form: gav mig sitt telefonnummer.
Possessives agree with the noun: vårt hus (ett-word) but vår bil (en-word).
hennes (her) never changes for gender or number: i hennes ögon.
You can stack sin with a genitive: sin dotters födelsedag = her own daughter's birthday.
A definite noun with an adjective takes a double marker: det stora trädet, both det and -et.
Double definiteness shows in both genders: den goda middagen (en) and det fina sällskapet (ett).
Adjectives add -t with ett-words: rummet var rent = the room was clean.
Adjectives add -a in the plural: svenska köttbullar = Swedish meatballs.
liten is irregular: en liten stuga, but ett litet, and små in the plural.
hela (whole) sits before the definite article: hela det stora bageriet.
Participles work as adjectives and take -a when definite: det sjunkna skeppet = the sunken ship.
närmaste is the superlative 'nearest': var ligger närmaste tunnelbanestation?
Add -s for possession, even on definite nouns: landets ekonomi = the country's economy.
dem is the object form of de (they): vi förde dem till hotellet.
under can mean 'during' for a time span: under lunchen = during lunch.
i veckan means 'per week': sex dagar i veckan = six days a week.
vänta på = wait for; the på is required: väntade på mig.
tycka om means to like; om is a stressed particle: vi tyckte om maten.
lyssna på = listen to; the på is required: jag lyssnade på henne.
medveten om = aware of; this adjective fixes its preposition as om: medveten om att han måste ändra.
Compass directions take om: norr om Uppsala = north of Uppsala.
in i = into, for movement inside: försvann in i skogen.
förbi means 'past/by': sprang förbi oss = ran past us.
checka in = check in; in is a separable particle after the verb: vi checkade in.
tillbaka (back) is a particle: ringa tillbaka = call back.
ihop = together, used as a particle: samlade ihop pengar = collected money.
As a particle, om can mean 're-' or 'again': måla om = repaint.
hinna med = manage to catch in time: hann inte med den = didn't make it.
åt marks who benefits: ett rum åt dig = a room for you.
med can mean 'by means of': med posten = by mail.
hit = to here (movement toward the speaker); här is the static 'here': komma hit.
hem = homeward (motion); hemma = at home (location): gick hem = went home.
nere = down as a location; ner is down as motion: nere vid hamnen.
framme means 'arrived/there': var vi framme = we had arrived.
härifrån = from here, combining här (here) and ifrån (from): busshållplats härifrån.
i morse = earlier this morning (already past); don't mix it up with i morgon = tomorrow.
i plus a weekday plus -s means 'last': i fredags = last Friday.
i marks a duration you spent: pratade i en timme = talked for an hour.
på plus a time span tells how long something took: på tre dagar = in three days.
förra = last/previous for time periods: förra våren = last spring.
varje means 'every' with a singular noun: varje morgon = every morning.
var before a time unit means 'every': var femtonde minut = every fifteen minutes.
klockan plus a number = at that o'clock: klockan sju = at seven.
det var länge sedan = it's been a long time since: länge sedan jag pratade svenska.
tycker states an opinion or taste; use tror for belief or a guess: vi tycker att filmen var bra.
tänka is to think in the sense of reckon or reflect: jag tänkte att det var du.
somna = fall asleep (the moment); sova = to sleep (the state): vi somnade sent.
Strong verbs change their vowel in the past: dricka becomes drack = drank.
se is irregular in the past: se becomes såg = saw: vi såg en film.
gråta is irregular in the past: gråta becomes grät = cried: hon grät.
Short verbs like sy take -dde in the past: sy becomes sydde = sewed.
betala takes the bill directly, with no 'for': betalade räkningen = paid the bill.
fråga takes the person as a direct object: frågade oss = asked us.
som tur var is a set phrase meaning 'luckily': som tur var hittade vi biljetten.
få reda på means to find out: fick reda på vad som hänt.
det var inte meningen is a set apology meaning 'I didn't mean to.'
vilken/vilket plus a noun makes an exclamation: Vilken otur = what bad luck.
Var is the imperative of vara (to be): Var försiktig = Be careful.
